checks.what: older fallers, two or more falls (FHm)
mean age of NF (y), the one age given as >89 counted as 90
one participant's age is top-coded (>89) in the register and left empty; the rest max at 89 or below
all 90 register participants have at least one recording here
every samples file has 3 x 26 channels x frames of 30 fps data, 9 to 40 s
units: centre-of-mass RMS distance from the cached skeleton (x100, 8 Hz low-pass) is within 0.7-1.8 times the authors' RDIST (median)

differences: The paper says participants were aged 18 to 92; the register's youngest is 23 and one age is given only as >89.

Only the recordings with a cached skeleton array or sway_metrics.csv in their folder are converted (roughly half of the 990 participant x movement recordings, mostly the standing and stance tests); the rest exist only as 180 GB of per-frame files.
The register has 47 male and 43 female participants; summing the sex columns of the paper's group table gives the same 47 male.

A few folders hold sway_metrics.csv files in an older layout (different column names); their values are used unchanged. The sway units are not stated in the paper; the authors' code labels them cm and the cached skeleton (metres) times 100 gives values of the same size as the sway files.
